intent: The editor screen, published by the design system. Named region slots (nav rail, left panel, canvas, inspector, timeline) the host fills; the shell owns the layout and the overlay boundary.
guidance: Fill the region slots and let the shell own the layout and the overlay boundary — the swap test is that changing one region moves nothing else. Omit the timeline slot for a tool that has none (a doc editor) and the shell reflows without it. The shell is a plain group, deliberately not role=application, so the inner landmarks (canvas = main, inspector = complementary) stay visible to assistive tech.

anatomy.description: Resizable left panel: composition, layers, assets, or agent.
The document surface — the only region that grows to fill space.
Bottom timeline strip. Optional — omit it for a tool with no timeline.
Floating chrome: toolbars, notifications, help, and portalled dialogs, within the shell's overlay boundary.

use_when: Assembling an editor screen from the DS instead of hand-writing the top-level layout.
You want the swap test: change one region and nothing else moves.
Building a second Figma-mental-model tool (e.g. a doc editor) — omit the timeline slot and reuse the same shell.
dont_use_when: You need a single panel, not a whole screen — use Inspector / PropertyPanel / Panel directly.
The region owns product or document state — that stays in the host; slots take rendered nodes.

overlayBoundary: true (default) — the workspace row is the DS overlay collision boundary
false — the host provides its own

slots.leftPanel: Resizable left panel: composition / layers / assets / agent.
slots.canvas: The document surface. The only region that grows.
slots.timeline: Bottom timeline strip. Optional — omit it for a tool with no timeline (doc editor).
slots.overlays: Floating chrome: toolbars, notifications, help, portalled dialogs.

tokens.surface: layout-only — no color or spacing tokens of its own; each slotted region carries its own

a11y.landmarks: slotted regions own their own landmarks (inspector = complementary, canvas = main); the shell is a plain group — deliberately NOT role=application, which would switch AT into application mode and hide those inner landmarks.
a11y.reading order: nav rail → left panel → canvas → inspector → timeline, matching the DOM.

code.example:
<EditorShell
  aria-label="Composa editor"
  navRail={<NavRail … />}
  leftPanel={<LeftPanel … />}
  canvas={<main aria-label="Canvas">…</main>}
  inspector={<Inspector>…</Inspector>}
  timeline={<Timeline … />}   /* omit for a doc editor */
  overlays={<><CreationToolbar … /><Notifications … /></>}
/>
